scope: Validation of forecasting methods on a Gaussian surrogate workload with known laws. Not a test of H2 or H2-R, not evidence about the path-integral sampler or about any random number generator, and not part of the Stage D pilot.
seed_recipe: rnglab.seeds.namespace_seed(namespace, set_name, role); roles: paths, noise, forward-simulation; bootstrap: namespace_seed(namespace, scenario, 'analysis', purpose)

alarm.threshold: 950th order statistic of the 999 calibration maxima

E_freeze.freeze: the run's own alarm sweep; the horizon when there is no alarm

forecasters.base-rate: training fraction valid among eligible training runs
forecasters.alarm-time: logistic regression on the alarm sweep
forecasters.lite-logistic: logistic regression on the alarm sweep, the statistic at the alarm and its slope over the last four checkpoints
forecasters.persistence: severity implied by the alarm-window statistic held from the middle of that window; estimated beta, sigma_eff, kappa
forecasters.bayes-ramp: posterior over the declared ramp parameters from the joint likelihood of the statistic history, mixed over the validity model; estimated beta, sigma_eff, kappa
forecasters.bayes-ramp-no-widening: the same with the drift-widening term of the validity model switched off (the noncentral-t formula)
forecasters.oracle: validity model at the true severity path with the estimated beta and sigma_eff; evaluation truth, a reference only

estimation.beta: training runs, least squares through the origin, exact reference used
estimation.kappa: training runs, least squares through the origin on the window-mean severity

eligibility: a run is scored at length L only if its alarm sweep is below L; counts of no alarm and late alarm are reported

failure_time.definition: first checkpoint from which the interval excludes the reference at 3 consecutive checkpoints

reading_rules.R1: Scenario A, bayes-ramp and oracle, each L: calibrated iff |Spiegelhalter Z| < 3 and count-weighted reliability gap (10 equal-width bins, bins with at least 50 runs) < 0.05. MET iff calibrated at all three L for both. Basis of the thresholds, fixed on development seeds before the freeze: for the oracle with the generating parameters and 2000 runs, 16 replicates gave |Z| at most 2.28 and a weighted gap at most 0.028.
reading_rules.R2: Scenario A, L = 20480: MET iff the 95% paired-bootstrap lower bound of the Brier skill of bayes-ramp over alarm-time is above 0.
reading_rules.R3: Scenario A, L = 20480: MET iff the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of Brier(bayes-ramp) - Brier(lite-logistic) lies entirely below 0.
reading_rules.R4: Scenario A, each L: the drift-widening term matters iff the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of Brier(bayes-ramp) - Brier(bayes-ramp-no-widening) lies entirely below 0. Reported per L; no overall label.
reading_rules.R5: Scenarios B1, B2, C, D: the R1 calibration rule and the Brier skill over alarm-time are reported for every forecaster and L. Expectation stated in advance: in C and in D, bayes-ramp fails the R1 rule at one L at least. The outcome is reported as EXPECTATION MET or NOT MET.
reading_rules.R6: Scenarios E: every forecast must be identical in the two worlds (exact equality; a difference is an implementation error and stops interpretation). Reported: Brier score of every forecaster in each world, the realised valid fractions, and the bound mean((p_continue - p_freeze)^2)/4 over eligible runs, with p from the validity model at the true paths and the generating parameters.
reading_rules.R7: Scenario A, failure time: MET iff the 95% paired-bootstrap lower bound of the ranked-probability-score skill of bayes-ramp over the empirical baseline is above 0. Coverage of the 80% central interval with its Clopper-Pearson interval, median errors, censoring counts and Kaplan-Meier medians are reported.
reading_rules.general: Every outcome is reported whichever way it falls. The study runs once. A code change after the freeze is an amendment written before the affected numbers are regenerated.
